briefs.headline: Alonso says Chelsea were not bullied at Sunderland but did not produce enough
briefs.summary: Xabi Alonso said Monday that Sunday's loss at the Stadium of Light was a situation Chelsea could have defended better rather than a case of being bullied, that the match was even until Enzo Le Fee's 36th-minute penalty and that his side did not produce enough once behind; asked about Brian Brobbey, who won the penalty off Levi Colwill and was substituted in the 67th minute, Alonso said the striker caused a few problems out of almost nothing and is stoppable with better defending. Pedro Neto started up front with Joao Pedro still out with a thigh injury, and Alonso said the international break would be used to get injured players back before Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 10 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Alisson says he is happy to stay as his agent talks to Liverpool over a new contract
briefs.summary: Alisson Becker, 34, in his ninth season at Anfield and due to become a free agent when his contract expires in June, said Monday that his will is to stay at Liverpool and that his agent is talking with the club, adding that he is still hungry for titles and has held no discussions himself with the hierarchy; Juventus were among the clubs linked with him in the summer. Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti has rested him for this window's friendlies against Japan and Singapore, and Alisson, who made six saves in Sunday's win at Crystal Palace, said the team's consistency under Andoni Iraola is not there yet and that it will take time. Liverpool next host Manchester United on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 11:30 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Browns plan to start Watson against Houston, a source tells ESPN, after Sanders' 297 yards
briefs.summary: The Browns plan to start Deshaun Watson at quarterback against the Texans on Sunday, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday, a day after Shedeur Sanders, starting with Watson not cleared from concussion protocol until Saturday, went 19 of 31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the overtime loss at New Orleans; coach Todd Monken said he was not ready to announce a starter and that he was proud of Sanders, who had not taken first-team reps in 10 weeks. ESPN noted Watson led Cleveland to five wins in eight games with an NFL-high five winning drives but entered Week 9 with a 40.9 QBR, 28th of 30 qualifying quarterbacks; Sanders' two 60-yard completions Sunday doubled Watson's total from his first eight games. Houston visits Huntington Bank Field on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Reds first baseman Sal Stewart wins the National League Rookie of the Year award
briefs.summary: Sal Stewart, 22, the Cincinnati Reds' first baseman, was named NL Rookie of the Year on Monday with 20 of 30 first-place votes from the Baseball Writers' Association of America, ahead of the Mets' Carson Benge (seven) and the Cardinals' JJ Wetherholt (three); Stewart hit 32 home runs with 112 RBIs, the first 30-homer, 100-RBI season by a Reds rookie, batted .263/.330/.457 with 15 stolen bases and played all 162 games, which he said was his greatest source of pride. Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle, 22, took the AL award with 28 of 30 first-place votes after leading the league with 7.1 Baseball-Reference WAR.

briefs.headline: Wembanyama scores 40 with 9 blocks in 25 minutes as San Antonio beats Phoenix 122-96
briefs.summary: Victor Wembanyama made 15 of 19 shots for 40 points, 11 rebounds and nine blocks and sat out most of the fourth quarter as San Antonio won a ninth straight game, 122-96 at Phoenix on Monday night; he had 22 points, six rebounds and five blocks by halftime as a run of 21 points to two built a lead of 61 to 46, Dylan Harper scored 14 of his 17 in a third quarter that stretched it to 93 to 68, and De'Aaron Fox added 15 with nine rebounds and six assists. Devin Booker scored 32 for the Suns, who shot 39.3% and were outrebounded 55 to 35; the Spurs have nine wins and two losses after losing their first two games and play at Chicago on Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Manchester United favor USMNT coach Pochettino to replace Carrick, ESPN reports
briefs.summary: ESPN reported late Monday, citing sources, that U.S. men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favored candidate to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United, with the club's leadership assessing Carrick after one win in 10 league games left United 18th, a point off the bottom; the sources said talks will continue over the coming days but that there is now acceptance that a change of manager is needed, and one source said Pochettino's U.S. Soccer contract, extended to 2030 in August after the World Cup round of 16, carries a $10 million release clause. ESPN named Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Kieran McKenna as other candidates; the USMNT plays Haiti in the first leg of a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal on Saturday in Miami at 4:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Fujiryoga pushes down Hoshoryu for his first kinboshi on day 3 of the Kyushu basho
briefs.summary: Maegashira (rank-and-file) 1 Fujiryoga, 23, in his first meeting with yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu, met the yokozuna's thrusts, unbalanced him when Hoshoryu reached for a right overarm grip and could not get it, and pushed him down over the edge by oshitaoshi (push down) in the final bout of day 3 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center, Hoshoryu's first loss since returning from three tournaments out with a right knee injury; Fujiryoga, who had lost both his previous bouts against a yokozuna, both to Onosato, and now has two wins and a loss, said attacking forward without pausing was what worked, and his kinboshi (gold star, a rank-and-filer's win over a yokozuna) came 11 tournaments and three days after his debut at makushita 60 in March 2025, the seventh-fastest for a wrestler who entered through the tsukedashi (amateur-credit) route. Japan Sumo Association chairman Hakkaku said the yokozuna's legs are not yet fully right and called it the effect of the injury.

briefs.headline: Onosato forces down Asanoyama, but Kirishima loses to Yoshinofuji and no yokozuna or ozeki is unbeaten
briefs.summary: Yokozuna Onosato, chasing a second straight yusho (championship), took his right inside grip against maegashira 1 Asanoyama's left overarm hold, stayed on him and turned him down by yoritaoshi (force out and down) for a second win, denying the former ozeki (champion) a first kinboshi in seven years; komusubi Yoshinofuji, day 1's conqueror of Onosato, threw ozeki Kirishima by uwatenage (overarm throw) after Kirishima went for a leg-hooking throw that NHK's Mainoumi called forceful and reckless, Kirishima's first loss, while ozeki Aonishiki forced out Ura and ozeki Kotozakura threw Fujiseiun. Mitonoumi, 33, the first wrestler from Okinawa to reach sanyaku (the titled ranks), beat sekiwake Fujinokawa with a left overarm throw for his first win as a komusubi, a third straight loss for the 21-year-old ozeki hopeful, who false-started twice, and Sponichi counted four men unbeaten after three days, sekiwake Atamifuji, who pushed out Daieisho, and Takanosho among them.

briefs.headline: Kotoeiho withdraws with a neck disc injury, the 3rd kyujo in the top two divisions
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association published a medical certificate Tuesday for maegashira 6 Kotoeiho, 23, diagnosing cervical disc herniation and about four weeks of rest, and he withdrew from day 3 with a win and a loss, giving Kinbozan a win by default; it is the third kyujo (absence) among sekitori (the top two divisions) this tournament after Shirokuma and Hishoshi. Tamawashi, 41, pushed out Daiseizan, 26, in his 1,500th top-division appearance for a second win a day after passing Kisenosato on the all-time list; maegashira 12 Abi, with one win in three after losing to Asasuiryu, said tests on the right ankle he hurt Monday showed a sprain and no bone damage and that he would not withdraw. In juryo (the second division), Wakatakakage forced out Shonannoumi for a third straight win in his first tournament since four operations on his left leg.

briefs.headline: Bills beat the Vikings 23-6 as Wentz goes 8 of 25 and Allen ties Manning's 10-year mark
briefs.summary: Josh Allen threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds left in the first half, James Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards and a late score, and Tyler Bass kicked three field goals, his 24th straight, as Buffalo held the ball for 42:32 and moved to 7-1, its best eight-game start since 1993; Allen, 21 of 31 for 234 yards with an interception, reached 322 regular-season touchdowns, tying Peyton Manning for the most in a player's first 10 seasons. Carson Wentz, starting for the injured Kyler Murray, went 8 of 25 for 81 yards with two interceptions and a lost fumble before Max Brosmer replaced him, Minnesota (6-2) finished with 178 yards and no touchdown for the third time this season, and coach Kevin O'Connell deferred to general manager Nolan Teasley on whether the Vikings would add a quarterback before today's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline.

briefs.headline: Jaguars add Bates, Godchaux and Davis a day before the 4 p.m. ET trade deadline
briefs.summary: Jacksonville traded on Monday for safety Jessie Bates III, defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and defensive tackle Jordan Davis, and Detroit added safety Andre Cisco, per ESPN's deadline tracker, which lists Jeffery Simmons to Chicago, J.J. McCarthy to the Giants, Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore and Joey Porter Jr. to Dallas among the in-season deals already done; trades must be approved by 4 p.m. ET today. New England, meanwhile, expects running back Rhamondre Stevenson to miss a few weeks with a knee tendon injury that is not expected to need surgery, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

briefs.headline: Flagg scores 43 and Irving 35 as the Mavericks rally past the Pacers 125-122
briefs.summary: Cooper Flagg had 43 points and 10 rebounds, his fourth straight double-double, and Kyrie Irving scored 35 with a season-high seven 3-pointers in 38 minutes, his first back-to-back since returning from a 19-month ACL absence, as Dallas scored the first 13 points of the fourth quarter and outscored Indiana 35 to 29 in it; Pascal Siakam scored 26 of his 29 before halftime for the Pacers, who led by 13, and Rick Carlisle argued with the officials at midcourt that a Dallas foul had gone uncalled on the final possession. The Mavericks, with seven wins and four losses, are three games over .500 for the first time since March 2025; the Pacers have three wins and eight losses.

briefs.headline: Doncic's 32 points and 10 assists carry the Lakers past the Hawks 124-114 for a 6th straight win
briefs.summary: Luka Doncic had 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists, Walker Kessler 21 points and 10 rebounds with three alley-oop dunks, and Sandro Mamukelashvili 23 points on 5-of-8 3-point shooting as Los Angeles, playing without Austin Reaves because of illness a day after his 43 at Detroit, built a 20-point second-quarter lead and answered Atlanta's late push to 115-111 with a run of six straight points; CJ McCollum scored 21 and Nickeil Alexander-Walker 20 for the Hawks, whose four-game winning streak ended. The Lakers have 10 wins and two losses and lead the Western Conference by half a game over the Spurs; they play at Milwaukee on Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Warriors rout the Pelicans 138-87 for an 8th straight win as Curry passes DeRozan
briefs.summary: Stephen Curry scored 25 in just over 20 minutes and moved past DeMar DeRozan into 16th on the career scoring list with 26,803 points, Brandin Podziemski added 25 and Yaxel Lendeborg 23 as Golden State led 35 to 20 after a quarter and 72 to 43 at halftime against a New Orleans team resting Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III; the Warriors had 37 assists, their third straight game of 30 or more, and led by as many as 51. Golden State lost guard Will Richard to a torn ligament in his left thumb and sent Brandon Williams for an MRI on a hamstring; the Warriors have eight wins and three losses and visit San Antonio on Friday in NBA Cup play.

briefs.headline: Draisaitl scores twice as the Oilers beat the Rangers 3-1; McDavid's point streak reaches 19
briefs.summary: Connor McDavid opened the scoring on an unassisted goal 6:42 into the first period after Dylan Garand gave the puck away, Leon Draisaitl snapped in his NHL-best 17th at 2:59 of the second and lofted his 18th into an empty net from his own zone with the Rangers skating 6-on-4 late, and Devon Levi made 28 saves to improve to 8-1-0 as Edmonton (13-3-3) swept the season series; McDavid, who leads the league with 48 points, became the fourth player with a 19-game point streak to open a season, after Wayne Gretzky, Dany Heatley and Mats Sundin, though his record run of 18 straight games with an assist ended. Jaroslav Chmelar scored short-handed for New York (10-8-1), which is 0-7-1 when allowing the first goal.

prime.limit: 18-inch minimum, 27-inch maximum total length; 1 per person per day
prime.item: Prime. The NCDMF table reads red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one fish per person per day, with note (C) making it unlawful to possess a red drum over 27 inches or to gig, spear or gaff one; the Fisherman's Post November report has the piers' 32-inch-plus fish on the north end of the island, which are over the slot and go back. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, which states it is effective Nov. 1, 2026, read this morning at 5:44 a.m.; the fisheries management proclamations list, read at the same time, showed no finfish proclamation issued since Oct. 30, the newest item still SF-2-2026, a shellfish proclamation of Nov. 5 on oyster mechanical harvest sites that takes effect Nov. 16. A Coastal Recreational Fishing License is required.

waters.reading: 45.3 cfs, 1.26 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on flow against 52.4 cfs and steady on stage against 1.32 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Against Monday's edition reading of 48.8 cfs and 1.29 feet at 5:15 a.m. the gauge is down 3.5 cfs and 0.03 feet on the day, and the recession took two more steps: the USGS record held 48.8 from Monday morning, traded it with 47.6 from 8 a.m. through the middle of the day, dropped to 46.5 at 6 p.m., reached 45.3 at 10:45 p.m. with one 15-minute return to 46.5 at 11, and has held 45.3 since 11:45 p.m.; the stage went 1.29, 1.28, 1.27, 1.26 on the same steps. The fetcher's 24-hour comparison figures, 52.4 and 1.32, are Sunday morning's values, a 48-hour window, so the day's true change is the 3.5 cfs above. At 45.3 the Williams is at the lowest reading of the fall for a third straight morning, under Monday's 48.8 and Sunday's 52.4, on a slide this paper has recorded from 1,360 cfs on Oct. 15 through 653 on Oct. 17, 141 on Oct. 24 and 70.7 on Oct. 31. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, printed as it stands, "45 cfs - prime wading water." Stocking: WVDNR's trout-stocking page answered this morning's fetch with a redirect and no body, so no stocking line runs; the river's most recent stocking this paper has reported is Oct. 29. At 45 cfs and clear the Williams is the file's low-water problem a notch lower again: pocket water and plunge pools shrunk to their cores, every fish in the deepest slot of each pocket, the water cold and glass-clear, and a wading angler the loudest thing on the river. Structure is pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks; forage is caddis, stoneflies and sculpin. So: a long leader, nine to 12 feet to 6X or 7X, and small flies, a size 16 to 18 caddis pupa or a size 18 soft-hackle swung into the plunge-pool tailouts, a size 16 to 18 pheasant tail or small black stonefly nymph under a tiny indicator or a dry-dropper through the pocket seams, a size 20 to 22 blue-winged olive on top through the warmest part of the afternoon, and for the one bigger fish in each plunge pool a size 8 to 10 olive or black sculpin pattern fished on a short line into the foam at the head of the pool at first or last light, before the sun gets on it; an egg pattern or a San Juan worm under a small indicator still covers the holdover stocked pools. The heavy-nymph-on-the-seam game is for 500 cfs, a number this river has not seen since the 653 of Oct. 17.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.32 feet at 5 a.m., rising against 24.54 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.3 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Monday's edition reading of 24.69 at 5 a.m. the pool is up 0.63 on the day: the trace drifted between 24.52 and 24.68 through Monday's daylight, bottoming at 24.52 at 1:45 p.m., turned up from 24.67 at 5 p.m. to 24.83 at 6:30, 25.09 at 9, 25.27 at 10:30 and 25.33 at midnight, reached 25.43 at 2:45 a.m. Tuesday and eased back to 25.32 at 5 a.m. The Williams fell all day, so the rise is not the hills on this side of the state; whether it is the dam holding water back overnight, as it did Sunday afternoon, or water coming down from upstream, the trace does not say and this paper will not guess. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, 25.3 feet and rising, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 25.3 the gauge is still 1.7 feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27. A pool that came up six-tenths overnight and is still in normal band fishes the structure, not the slack: wing dams, riprap and the lock wall are the file's structure, shad and skipjack with crawfish in the rock the forage. A white or pearl three-and-a-half to four-inch swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of each wing dam at first light for hybrids and white bass; a crawfish-colored jig or a three-inch tube dragged slow on the riprap through the middle of the day for smallmouth and drum; and with the water cooling through November a half-ounce blade bait or a jig and minnow worked vertical along the lock wall seam and the barge-cut edges for sauger, cut skipjack on the bottom in the cuts after dark for blue catfish. A rising pool pushes bait up onto the flooded rock and the flats behind the wing dams through the morning, which puts the first hour of light on the inside edges of the dams rather than the current faces.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.22 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.18 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.2 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Monday's edition reading of 26.28 at 5 a.m. the gauge is down 0.06 on the day, and the day in between was a round trip: the trace fell from 26.23 at 6:45 a.m. Monday through 26.05 at 9:15, 25.88 at noon and 25.80 at 6 p.m. to 25.79 at 7 p.m., then climbed back through 26.00 at 11:30 p.m., 26.10 at 1:15 a.m. and 26.24 at 4:15 a.m. to 26.22 at 5 a.m. Tuesday. The dam below tells most of it: the USGS gauge at Ironton, Ohio, below Greenup Dam, recorded Greenup's discharge between 20,300 and 25,100 cfs through Monday morning, cut to 11,800 to 15,800 through the early afternoon and 7,850 at 3:45 p.m., back to 18,000 at 6 p.m., 12,200 to 22,800 through the evening and 20,300 to 25,700 after 1 a.m., 24,000 at 5 a.m. Tuesday; the Ironton stage ran from 34.44 at 6:45 a.m. Monday down to 34.20 at 2:15 p.m. and up to 34.56 at 5 a.m. Tuesday. So Greenup throttled back Monday afternoon and the Huntington reach dropped half a foot with the Ironton pool, then both came back overnight as the dam passed more water, while the Byrd pool above rose six-tenths; the two gauges are moving together again this morning, and neither trace says rain. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. Below the dam the reach is back where it was Monday morning with Greenup drawing 24,000 cfs below, a little more push on the seams than Monday evening's slack, and the fishing goes to them: a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of the wing dams at first light for hybrids and white bass, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head worked slow along the lock wall's downstream edge for sauger, a crawfish jig on the riprap at midday, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the slack beside the discharge after dark for blue and flathead catfish. No color in either trace; the slack-behind-the-dams game is for a muddy river, not this one.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 2:22 AM at 0.4 ft, high 8:31 AM at 4.2 ft, low 3:11 PM at 0.7 ft, high 8:45 PM at 3.3 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 1:00 AM at 0.3 ft, high 7:37 AM at 5.4 ft, low 2:05 PM at 0.4 ft, high 7:54 PM at 3.8 ft. Water 65.5F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon new, 0% illuminated, 0.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 8:31 AM and 8:45 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All four of the sound's events land inside the calendar day, the 2:22 a.m. low behind us at press time, and so do the surf's, the 1:00 a.m. low at Ocean City Beach pier having come an hour and 22 minutes ahead of the sound's; the sound lags the surf 54 minutes on the morning high, 66 on the midday low and 51 on the evening high, the long-lag-on-the-ebb pattern the reference describes. The ranges are at the top of the cycle: a 3.8-foot fill overnight from 0.4 to this morning's 4.2, a 3.5-foot drain to 3:11 p.m., a 2.6-foot fill to the 8:45 p.m. high, which at 3.3 is a tenth under Monday's evening high, and the surf's 5.4 morning high is a tenth under Monday's; the moon is new, half a day old at 0%, so these are spring tides at their peak and the inlet runs hardest either side of slack, with the whole table 41 to 43 minutes later than Monday's. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, reads 65.5F, down 0.2 on Monday's 65.7 and 2.7 under Saturday's 68.2, a third straight morning of cooling after a night of frost advisories inland. What's running: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report for November, published Sunday, Nov. 1, is nine days old this morning, a monthly report and not today's conditions. It has the Jolly Roger Pier starting to see scattered speckled trout, with night bottom fishing producing Virginia mullet and spot and bluefish thick in the early mornings; Surf City Pier with pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom, casting shots at Spanish and bluefish, and king mackerel good before the last blow; East Coast Sports with the piers catching big red drum of 32 inches and more, mostly on the north end, smaller reds and some trout inside, and trout to pick up as it cools; Native Son with the wind scattering bait, the five- to eight-foot seams of the main creeks the depth to work for trout, cut bait the best red drum bait, and false albacore possible; Capt. Ricky Kellum with many small specks and some to 28 inches on live shrimp under a cork in four to eight feet of water, 3/16-ounce jigheads for the artificials, and black drum to 18 inches and small reds on the same floated shrimp over structure; Carolina Flats with topwater early to find the trout schools, deeper holes later, and reds in a last blitz on the oyster and grass banks on soft plastics before the bait thins; and the boats with kings on slow-trolled bait in 50 to 60 feet, bluefish, false albacore and gray trout on nearshore structure, sea bass and triggerfish on the bottom in 60 to 80 feet. Beach conditions: no NWS Wilmington product was active for coastal Pender or Onslow, the Topsail point or the adjacent marine zones at 5:44 a.m.; the only North Carolina products on the wire were Frost Advisories to 7 or 8 a.m. from the Raleigh, Newport/Morehead City and Wakefield offices for inland counties, Inland Onslow among them and not the coast. Tide is the whole game, and this morning it is the last of the flood at press time: the sound fills to 4.2 at 8:31 a.m. and then drains for six hours and 40 minutes to the 3:11 p.m. low, the long morning ebb of the new-moon tide. Structure here is oyster bars, grass edges, dock lights and the ICWW channel, forage mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet, which is the report's live-shrimp-and-small-plastic fishing. Trout first: a topwater plug over the flooded grass edges in the first hour of light around the 8:31 a.m. high, then a 3/16- or quarter-ounce jighead with a paddletail or soft jerkbait worked slow down the five- to eight-foot seams where the creek channels drop into the ICWW as the drain gathers through late morning, and a popping cork with live shrimp over the oyster bars on the first of the flood after 3:30 p.m. and again either side of the 8:45 p.m. high; with the water at Beaufort at 65.5F and falling the trout hold the deeper holes on the midday low. Red drum want the last of the fall, which on this table is roughly 12:30 to the 3:11 p.m. low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges as the grass drains; the dusk high at 8:45 p.m. puts drum up on the flooded grass and oyster banks for a weedless gold spoon or a soft plastic, and the ebb that follows runs under the dock lights past 2 a.m., the report's small plastics or a suspending twitchbait where the shrimp and finger mullet stack. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel an hour either side of the evening high. Bluefish are the early-morning fish on the beach behind the bait pods on a metal jig or topwater, per both piers. Flounder are release only.
